doc.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021

title: Art-form status, losing dancers and the audience
summary: Calling jazz an art form separated it from popular music and dancing, so the audience went to R&B and rock; danceable styles remain popular.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Can we pursue that a little bit? About the art form. Because I’ve been fascinated by that over the years and that it kind of went hand in hand with losing much of the audience it seems like, once jazz became an art form it lost some popularity and became almost like classical music is in the United States.

The thing about art form is fine if you’re going after grants or you want Congress to declare jazz you know America’s National Treasure. That’s all nice. But when it comes to building up an audience I mean jazz is basically the most fun music in the world, it’s the most adventurous music. You know the idea of seeing someone, seeing a group come on stage and make up the music as they go along, which in some more advanced areas of jazz it’s practically free improvisation. That’s exciting, it’s must more exciting to me than seeing a pop group try to recreate their records on stage, you know with a captive audience. And that the problem with jazz being declared an art form, it was fine in the 40s, you know because you know they were trying to separate jazz from popular music. But by doing that you end up separating jazz from popular music and you know jazz got rid of the — for a variety of reasons jazz was no longer being played for dancers even though the music itself is danceable much of the time. And by doing that you lost a lot of

the audience. You know the audience went to rhythm & blues and eventually rock & roll and Motown and everything else. And if you look at what the most popular music in the world is generally it’s danceable music. Even in jazz, one of the most popular styles, well Latin jazz you know, and swing is still popular, and there are some parts of fusion that are rock oriented was danceable. That’s much more popular than bebop or hard bop, and yet bebop and hard bop are danceable, it’s just that it’s not danceable if you don’t have a dance floor.

That’s true. I love the practical considerations that come into what happens to music. “Well I could dance to it but there’s no music because this place seats like 40 people and there’s no place to move around.”
No. You can’t dance to it if there’s nowhere to dance.
